page.overview:
Who is Isaia Bendikt?

Isaia Bendikt was a Cadian general of the Astra Militarum who commanded the regiments of the Cadian Shock Troops and survived the Fall of Cadia to take part in the Battle of Faith's Anchorage and to found a colony and sanctuary for Cadian survivors on the seventh world of the Agripinaa System he renamed "New Cadia."

Before the start of the 13th Black Crusade and the Fall of Cadia, Bendikt was a major in the Cadian 101st Armoured Regiment and served during the Deucalion Crusade commanded by Warmaster Ryse. During that Imperial Crusade, Bendikt led the 101st Armoured to become the most decorated of all Cadian armoured regiments. Bendikt himself was twice awarded the Valorous Unit Citation and shared with his tank crew six Steel Crosses, four Steel Aquila and the Order of the Eagle's Claw. Despite his decorated career, Bendikt was shocked to learn that Ursarkar E. Creed, an officer like him lacking any aristocratic family background, had been promoted through the ranks to become a general, even though their careers in the Astra Militarum had begun at the same time.

Once he was able to overcome his initial jealousy concerning Creed's promotion, Bendikt began to study Creed's tactics and followed the other man's career through various memos sent from Cadian High Command and regimental dispatches. When an increase in Chaos activity in the region of the Cadian Gate led the Imperium to call for a muster of its forces on Cadia, Bendikt's troops were among the forces that Warmaster Ryse brought to the Fortress World. As he waited aboard the Warmaster's flagship, the Fidelitas Vector, for the window to land, Bendikt had a chance to actually meet with Creed and congratulate him for his promotion. He was surprised when Creed actually recognised his name and actually proceeded to list the honours he had earned in the Deucalion Crusade. Their conversation did not end before Creed claimed that Cadian High Command was underestimating the Chaos threat the Imperium faced in the region and it would be up to Guardsmen like Bendikt and himself to keep the Cadian Gate safe.

Bendikt and the 101st Cadian Armoured were then deployed to Cadia, but they were not sent to the city of Kasr Tyrok with the majority of the Imperial muster's forces. Instead they were dispatched, without their tanks, to the remote Observation Post 9983 in the Cadian mountains. Without the Valkyries that had shuttled them to the post but had quickly departed, the regiment had no way to leave the Observation Post and the skeleton crew at the post was unable to explain their purpose for having been sent there. This marked the start of a period of great frustration for Bendikt, an impatience that only increased with the start of the 13th Black Crusade.
